title: Personal Information Identification
description: During account registration, the homeowner provides personally identifiable information (name, address, contact details) that can be used to identify them.
uncertainty_note: Node ID I.1.1 is based on general LINDDUN knowledge; exact node may vary.

title: Unauthorized Data Access
description: Personal data stored by the Home Hub could be accessed by unauthorized parties through security vulnerabilities or insider threats.
uncertainty_note: Node ID D.1.1 is based on general LINDDUN knowledge; exact node may vary.

title: Metadata Linkability
description: Metadata about the data flow (timestamps, device identifiers) could be used to link the homeowner to other data or services.
uncertainty_note: Node ID L.1.1 is based on general LINDDUN knowledge; exact node may vary.

title: Unintended Data Usage
description: Camera/sensor data collected during enrollment could be used for purposes beyond the homeowner's consent, such as marketing or third-party sharing.
uncertainty_note: Node ID U.1.1 is based on general LINDDUN knowledge; exact node may vary.

title: Data Tampering
description: Registration data could be altered during transmission between Homeowner and Home Hub, potentially leading to incorrect account setup or security vulnerabilities.
uncertainty_note: Node ID Dd.1.1 is based on general LINDDUN knowledge; exact node may vary.

title: Linkability of guest access code
description: The home hub could potentially link the temporary access code to other guest information or activities, enabling profiling or tracking of the guest's association with the home.

title: Identification of guest through access code
description: The temporary access code could be used to identify the guest, potentially revealing their identity or association with the home to unauthorized parties.

title: Interception of access code in transit
description: The temporary access code could be intercepted during transmission to the home hub, allowing unauthorized parties to gain access to the home.

title: Insecure storage of access code
description: The home hub could store the temporary access code insecurely, allowing unauthorized access to stored codes and potential unauthorized entry.

title: Coercion of guest to share access code
description: The guest could be coerced, tricked, or socially engineered into sharing the temporary access code with unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized Access to Local Event Log
description: The local event log (DS1) may be accessible to unauthorized parties, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensor events including motion, door, and sensor data that could reveal household activities and presence patterns.

title: Identification of Individuals from Event Data
description: The event log contains data that could be used to identify specific individuals, such as door open/close events indicating when people enter or leave the home, and motion events showing presence in specific areas.

title: Linkability of Events to Build Activity Profile
description: Multiple events in the log can be linked together to create a detailed profile of household activities, including daily routines, presence patterns, and behavioral habits.

title: Lack of User Awareness/Consent for Data Collection
description: The Home Hub (P1) may be collecting sensor events without explicit user awareness or consent, particularly if users are not informed about what data is being logged and how it will be used.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Video data and metadata could be intercepted during transmission from Home Hub to Cloud Video Storage, potentially revealing who is being recorded and when.

title: Metadata Linkability in Transit
description: Transmission metadata (timestamps, device identifiers) could be used to link video recordings to specific individuals or locations.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Videos
description: Cloud Video Storage provider or unauthorized third parties could access stored video recordings without proper authorization.

title: Unintended Use of Stored Surveillance Data
description: Cloud storage provider could use video data for purposes beyond the intended surveillance function, such as profiling or selling to third parties.

title: Excessive Data Retention
description: Video recordings may be retained longer than necessary, increasing the risk of unauthorized access and potential misuse.

title: Source Compromise Before Upload
description: Home Hub device could be compromised before upload, allowing attackers to intercept or alter video data at the source.

title: Unauthorized Identification During Data Transmission
description: Motion alert data transmitted in real-time could be intercepted by third parties, enabling unauthorized identification of the user's location, activities, or presence at specific times.

title: Unauthorized Linkability of Motion Events
description: Metadata or motion event data in transit could be used to link the user to specific locations, times, or patterns of behavior, potentially revealing privacy-sensitive information about daily routines.

title: User Unawareness of Motion Data Collection
description: Users may not be fully aware that their home hub is collecting and forwarding real-time motion data to external systems, leading to unexpected privacy implications.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure at Destination
description: The mobile app backend may store, process, or share motion data in ways that expose it to unauthorized parties, systems, or third parties without proper access controls.

title: Linkability of motion patterns to homeowner presence
description: Motion-detected notifications transmitted in transit could be analyzed to link the homeowner's presence/absence patterns across time, potentially revealing daily routines, work schedules, or when the home is unoccupied.

title: Identification of homeowner through notification metadata
description: Metadata about the notification (timing, frequency, content) could be used to identify the specific homeowner and infer their location patterns, even if the notification itself is not directly identifying.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of presence information to third parties
description: The homeowner's device or the notification system could be compromised, leading to unauthorized disclosure of when the homeowner is present or absent from their home to third parties.

title: Excessive data collection for notification purposes
description: The mobile app backend may be collecting motion detection data that exceeds what is necessary for simply sending a notification, potentially capturing more detailed behavioral information than required.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics transmitted between mobile app backend and cloud analytics vendor could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, potentially exposing sensitive usage patterns and device information.

title: Metadata Linkability in Transit
description: Metadata accompanying the analytics data (such as timestamps, device identifiers, or request patterns) could be used to link or identify users across different data flows or sessions, even if the data itself is aggregated.

title: De-anonymization of Aggregated Data
description: The cloud analytics vendor may possess additional data or context that could be used to re-identify individual users from the supposedly aggregated device-usage analytics, violating user privacy expectations.

title: Unauthorized Data Usage Beyond Agreement
description: The cloud analytics vendor may use the received analytics data for purposes beyond the original agreement (e.g., selling to third parties, training AI models, or profiling users) without user consent or knowledge.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Analytics
description: Once received, the analytics data stored by the cloud analytics vendor may be accessible to unauthorized personnel or systems within the vendor's infrastructure, leading to potential data breaches.

title: Linkability via Video Metadata
description: Metadata embedded in or accompanying the video transmission (e.g., timestamps, device identifiers, location data) could be used to link the video to the homeowner's identity or other data points, potentially revealing patterns of behavior or presence.

title: Identification via Video Content
description: The video content itself may contain identifiable information about the homeowner, their property, or their activities, which could be used to identify them to unauthorized observers during transmission.

title: Disclosure During Transmission
description: Video data in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties through network eavesdropping or man-in-the-middle attacks, leading to unauthorized disclosure of the video content.

title: Identification by Backend Processing
description: The mobile app backend could extract and store identifiable information from the video (e.g., facial recognition, property details) that could be used to identify the homeowner beyond the intended playback purpose.

title: Unauthorized Storage or Sharing by Backend
description: The mobile app backend could improperly store, cache, or share the video with third parties or other systems without proper authorization or consent.

title: Linkability of Video to Other Data
description: The backend could link this video to other data about the homeowner (e.g., access logs, other stored videos, user profiles) creating a comprehensive profile that exceeds the intended purpose.

title: Identification via Access Request
description: The act of requesting and sharing the video from cloud storage could reveal ownership information or access patterns that identify the homeowner to the cloud storage system or its administrators.

title: Disclosure from Improper Access Controls
description: The cloud storage system may have inadequate access controls, allowing unauthorized access to the video data before it is properly transmitted to the mobile app backend.
